source_text: Liberum arbitrium non perisse, cum loquatur Dominus per Prophetam: Si volueritis et audieritis me, quae bona sunt terrae edetis; si nolueritis et non audieritis, gladius vos comedet. Ac per hoc et gratiam adiuvare uniuscuiusque bonum propositum, non tamen reluctanti studium virtutis immittere, quia personarum acceptio non est apud Deum
pass_a_gloss: that free decision has not perished, since the Lord speaks through the Prophet: If you are willing and listen to me, you will eat the good things of the land; if you are unwilling and do not listen, the sword will eat you. And accordingly grace also helps each one's good purpose, yet does not send in the pursuit of virtue to one who resists, because there is no acceptance of persons with God.

lemmas.lexica: LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere
LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium

pass_b_english: Free will has not been lost, since the Lord says through the prophet: “If you are willing and listen to me, you will eat the good things of the land; if you are unwilling and do not listen, the sword will eat you” (Isaiah 1:19–20). Accordingly, grace also helps each person’s good purpose, but does not plant the pursuit of virtue in someone who resists, because there is no partiality with God (Romans 2:11; Colossians 3:25).

choices.why: Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
In the suum cuique definition gratia is partiality, not saving grace.
Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

bible_refs.note: Linked from Julian's wording or a clear allusion in the excerpt.

speaker: Julian and fellow bishops (Collective letter to Thessalonica, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 2–4); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
kind: quotation preserved partly in indirect speech
